newsitem.title: USA: Gephardt says New Hampshire trip not primary bid.
newsitem.headline: Gephardt says New Hampshire trip not primary bid.

text.p: House Minority Leader Dick Gephardt Thursday paid a visit to the first-in-the-nation primary state but said that Congressional not presidential politics was the purpose of his trip.
"The future will take care of itself," the Missouri Democrat said as he declined to answer a reporter's question about his rumored presidential aspirations.
Gephardt said his mission to New Hampshire was about recruiting Democrats to run for Congress in 1998, as well as to make a courtesy call on newly elected Democratic Gov. Jeanne Shaheen.
Gephardt said Shaheen's election shows Democrats can make inroads in this traditional GOP bastion.

"We didn't win ... but we did well. Our two candidates for congress did very well. They were in close elections. Our candidate for the Senate did very well and was in a close election in a state that has traditionally been tough for us. That's good news," Gephardt said.
"If good candidates come forth and run competent campaigns, we can win here, we can win both seats," Gephardt said.
